reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: original ¶p0188 binds only Customer, offers a partial successor carve-out of ambiguous consent effect, and imposes no restriction on IBM's assignment.

Redline reaches the preferred position with targeted edits: it adds the affiliate/sale-of-substantially-all-assets carve-out expressly 'without IBM's consent' and inserts a reciprocal, reasonableness-qualified consent requirement on IBM with a Customer-competitor prohibition; existing void-assignment and continuing-liability sentences are preserved.
No change-of-control termination right against Customer appears in the cited text, so the absence of a deletion is consistent with the rule rather than an omission.

Comment is accurate, in-house voice, prefixed correctly, states what changed and why, and offers the playbook fallback (mutual successor assignment on written notice with reasonable consent for others).
Changed-character ratio (~0.50) is explained by the required insertion of a new reciprocal obligation and is not evidence of over-editing; deterministic checks otherwise pass.
